main.description: A dictionary entry of the Leksis dictionary. Records prove authorship, not ownership: any user may publish an entry record, and a record carrying a `subject` reference is a proposed new version of the entry that record belongs to — the AppView treats the latest version as current and archives previous ones. The record is the source of truth for its content; the AppView indexes only what search needs. The entry is homolingual: every piece of text it carries — definitions, notes, references — is written in the entry's own language (`languageID`), for a reader of that language. It carries no reader-facing labels of its own: those are tags, and the language record binds each one to a name in that language.

languageID.description: Well-formed IETF BCP 47 tag of the entry's language, normalized to lowercase (e.g. "br", "br-gw").

orthography.description: Valid spellings of the word: variants, archaic forms, regional spellings. The first item is the canonical form.

transcription.description: Phonetic transcription of the word in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), e.g. "[ˈbrɛːzɔ̃nɛk]". Record-only content, not indexed by the AppView.

categories.description: Ordered grammatical categories of the entry, as tags — machine identifiers, never reader-facing text. The label a reader sees comes from the language record, which binds each tag to a name in that language. Non-grammatical headword labels ("vulg.", "arch.", "fam.") are not categories: they go in `notes` as prose, or become tags in their own right once the language mints and binds a feature for them. Order is the entry author's. May be empty: a language whose grammar nobody has declared yet stays fully authorable.

otherForms.description: Other grammatical forms of the word (plural, gerund, construct state…), each a tag saying which form it is plus its spelling (e.g. Number=Plur + "bugale"). The label a reader sees comes from the language record, as it does for the entry's categories. The AppView indexes each form's spelling for search, so an inflected form leads back to its entry.

definitions.description: The entry's definitions as a flat list, each item a node of a hierarchy of up to three dimensions addressed by its `place`. A node whose place ends in a non-zero index is a leaf (the definition proper: it carries `text`); a node whose place ends in 0 is a group node (a heading that carries notes but no text — e.g. the "transitive" grouping over several senses). Bare grouping (a group with no notes) is left implicit — it need not appear as its own item; the hierarchy is inferred from the leaves. The array is sorted by `place` in reading order.

etymology.description: The word's history, as prose paragraphs written in the entry's own language — one item per paragraph, for a competing or complementary account as much as for a long one. Prose deliberately, and not a graph: a word's history is a chain of forms across historical languages, carrying dates, uncertainty, mechanisms whose borders blur (inherited, borrowed, calqued, derived) and disagreement between sources, and formalizing it would encode false precision while reading worse for the person the entry is for. What IS formalized is the simple, machine-checkable half of the same knowledge: that two words share an origin, asserted between entries as an eu.leksis.cognate record. So a historical form named in this prose becomes a cognate link once that language and that form have records of their own — the prose tells the story, the cognate network makes it traversable. Record-only content, not indexed by the AppView.

notes.description: Entry-level free-text notes shown below the definitions (usage remarks, provenance, editorial comments). Freeform prose, not abbreviations.

references.description: Bibliographic references and sources for the entry, shown at the bottom of the entry.

subject.description: AT URI of the entry record version this record modifies. Absent for a brand-new entry; present on a proposed modification, so the AppView can attach this version to the existing entry.

todo.description: Pending-work notes: each item is one task this version still needs (e.g. an ingestion bot flagging one unverified aspect), so several bots or editors can each track their own item. Empty or absent means nothing is pending. The AppView indexes only whether any item exists, as a boolean flag.

deleted.description: Marks this version as a deletion: the entry is withdrawn from search under this record, but stays reachable at its entryKey for legacy links and to contest the deletion. Requires `deletionReason`. `orthography`/`categories`/`definitions` still carry the version's last known content (or may repeat the prior version's), since the lexicon requires them, but the AppView excludes a deleted version's orthography from the search index.

deletionReason.description: Required when `deleted` is true: why this entry was withdrawn (e.g. "duplicate of br-gwerzenn-1b76", "not an attested word").

redirectTo.description: When `deleted` is true and the reason is a duplicate, the entryKey of the correct entry to redirect readers to.

createdAt.description: Client-declared creation time of this record version.

place.description: Address of the node in the entry's tree: one index per dimension, deepest last. The LAST index is the node type — non-zero means a leaf (the definition proper, so `text` is required), 0 means a group node (a heading carrying notes but no text). A non-last index of 0 means "no grouping at that dimension", so a place can render shallower than its length (e.g. [0,1,1] = I. 1., [1] = [0,1] = [0,0,1] = 1.). In display each non-zero index n shows as the n-th label of its dimension and each 0 is skipped; numbering by displayed depth: 1 → arabic; 2 → roman, arabic; 3 → letters, roman, arabic (so [1,2,0] = A. II., [1,1,1] = A. I. 1.). Across the entry, places are sorted in reading order and sibling indices are contiguous from 1.

categories.description: Grammatical tags of this sense — a verb is VERB at the entry level and transitive on one sense group, intransitive on another. Same type as the entry's `categories`, at a different altitude. Allowed on leaves and group nodes alike.

notes.description: Free-text remarks shown before the node's content — neither labels nor part of the definition text. Allowed on leaves and group nodes alike.

text.description: The definition text. Required on and only on a leaf (place ending in a non-zero index); a group node (place ending in 0) must not carry text.

examples.description: Sentences illustrating THIS sense, in the entry's own language. Allowed on a leaf only: an example exemplifies one meaning, and a group node is a heading with no meaning of its own to exemplify — the same asymmetry as `text`. A leaf may carry several, from several sources or from none.

example.description: One example sentence for a definition: the sentence, and optionally the work it was taken from.

text.description: The sentence itself, written in the entry's own language, as the entry's every other piece of text is. Long enough for a short passage rather than a single clause, because a citation that has to be truncated to fit stops attesting what it was quoted for.

source.description: The work this sentence was taken from, when it was taken from one. Absent means an unsourced example — constructed by the entry's author, or heard rather than read — which is a legitimate lexicographic object and not an incomplete citation.

exampleSource.description: Where an example sentence comes from: which work, and where in it. The work is referenced by its OCLC number rather than by the AT URI of an eu.leksis.source record, deliberately — the number is the work's identity, so the reference stays valid across every version of that record and is valid before anybody has published one at all. A citation can therefore only degrade (the reader sees the bare number), never break. Everything a reader sees of the work — the short and long citation forms — is rendered from the eu.leksis.source record for this number, so a mistyped citation is corrected once for every entry that quotes the work.

oclc.description: OCLC number of the cited work, in normal form: digits only, without the "(OCoLC)" wrapper, the "ocm"/"ocn"/"on" prefixes, or leading zeros. The same normal form an eu.leksis.source record is keyed on — that is what makes the two meet. No grapheme cap: the value is ASCII digits by construction.

locator.description: Where in the source the sentence is: "p. 142", "s.v. gwerzenn", "§4", "f. 12v", "14:03". Free text rather than a page number, because pagination, column, folio, headword and timestamp locators do not share a schema, and an integer field would be false precision the moment the source is a dictionary, a manuscript or a recording. Optional: a whole work is a legitimate source for a sentence (a proverb collection cited in bulk).

inflectedForm.description: One other grammatical form of the word: which form it is, and how it is spelled.

tag.description: Which form this is, as a tag — one bundle, because the tag is the form's address in the paradigm: a dictionary's "gen. pl." is one coordinate in two dimensions, so it carries Case=Gen and Number=Plur together. The values are the ones the language declares as `axes` of the entry's category, though nothing requires it: an axis declaration is a menu and never a whitelist, and a form matching no declared axis simply stays in the flat list.

form.description: The spelling of the inflected form (e.g. "bugale").

text.description: The reference's display text (a citation, source name or note).

url.description: Optional URL the reference links to.
